symptoms: We have a major outage spanning our worldwide infrastructure.
Errors are coming back from the vast majority of our network.
Our alerts fired almost as soon as the failure began.
visible_during_incident.affected_service: Our worldwide content delivery infrastructure at the edge
visible_during_incident.dependent_impact: Clients and their end users are experiencing failures in the services that depend on us.
visible_during_incident.scope: Worldwide impact across well over three quarters of our network.
visible_during_incident.timing: The failure appeared abruptly in the morning UTC, with alerts following almost immediately.
already_tried: Our alerts picked up the failure almost immediately.
During troubleshooting, we pinpointed a client-side configuration of interest roughly forty minutes into the outage, while recovery was still pending.

complete_message: Our worldwide edge infrastructure has abruptly started failing, with errors coming from the vast majority of the network. Alerts fired almost immediately after the first failures. We have not established whether anything changed just beforehand.

conversation.analyst: It is our worldwide edge infrastructure that delivers content. Well over three quarters of it is producing errors.
We have not established whether anything changed just beforehand.
Failures appeared abruptly in the morning UTC, and alerts followed almost immediately. Most of our worldwide infrastructure is affected, along with clients and their end users.
Errors are coming back from the vast majority of our network worldwide. Our alerts corroborate the broad impact.

discovered_later.root_cause: A previously undiscovered software bug had been introduced during an earlier software deployment. The bug could be triggered by a specific customer configuration under specific circumstances. A customer pushed a valid configuration change that met those conditions, triggering the bug and causing 85% of the global network to return errors.
fix: Identified and isolated the triggering customer configuration.
Disabled the configuration responsible for triggering the bug.
Impacted services began recovering at 10:36 UTC.
Approximately 95% of the network was operating normally within 49 minutes of the initial disruption.
The majority of services had recovered by 11:00 UTC, and the incident was mitigated at 12:35 UTC.
Developed a permanent software fix and began deploying it at 17:25 UTC.
prevention: Deploy the permanent bug fix across the network as quickly and safely as possible.
Conduct a complete post-mortem review of the processes and practices followed during the incident.
Investigate why software quality assurance and testing processes failed to detect the bug.
Evaluate ways to improve incident remediation time.
Invest in fundamental platform resilience improvements, leveraging WebAssembly isolation capabilities.
discovered_later.changes: An earlier software deployment introduced the latent bug. A later valid customer configuration change triggered it. During mitigation, the triggering configuration was disabled. A permanent software bug fix was developed, and deployment began at 17:25 UTC. The post-mortem does not specify the exact code or configuration changes.
